next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — 2026 Election Information

glance_notes.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Registering to Vote
glance_notes.text: Same-Day Registration Available: Nevada allows eligible voters to register or update their registration during early voting and on Election Day. Voters using same-day registration in person must provide the identification and proof of residency required by Nevada law.

glance_notes.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Early Voting Information
glance_notes.text: Early Voting: Nevada provides in-person early voting before statewide elections. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the statutory early-voting period runs from Saturday, October 17 through Friday, October 30. Locations and hours are established by county election officials.

glance_notes.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Mail Ballot Voting
glance_notes.text: Mail Ballots Sent Automatically: Nevada generally sends a mail ballot automatically to each active registered voter for statewide elections unless the voter has opted out of receiving mail ballots. Voters may still choose to vote in person.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Nevada residents may register online through the Secretary of State's voter registration system, by mail, in person through county election officials and through qualifying automatic voter registration transactions. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old by Election Day and have continuously resided in Nevada and the applicable county for at least 30 days and in the applicable precinct for at least 10 days before the election. Nevada also allows eligible 17-year-olds who will be 18 by the General Election to participate in the corresponding Primary Election. Eligible residents who miss the ordinary registration deadlines may use Nevada's same-day registration procedures during early voting or on Election Day.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, automatic and same-day registration
register.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Registering to Vote
register.internal_note: Nevada Constitution Article 2 and NRS Chapter 293 establish the citizenship, age and residency requirements. Nevada allows same-day registration and registration updates after ordinary registration closes. Current Nevada law also permits a person who will be 18 by the General Election to vote in the associated Primary Election. Nevada automatically restores voting rights for a person convicted of a felony upon release from prison; no separate application is required.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Nevada's official voter registration system to check your registration status and update eligible registration information online. Voters can also contact their county election office for registration records, polling locations, mail-ballot information and other voter-specific questions.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through Nevada's voter registration system
check_registration.internal_note: RegisterToVoteNV is Nevada's official statewide online voter registration service. County election officials remain the appropriate authority for voter-specific local election information.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Nevada's ordinary registration deadlines occur before Election Day, but eligible residents who miss them are not necessarily prevented from voting. Nevada permits extended online registration and same-day registration during early voting and on Election Day. A voter registering in person during the same-day registration period must provide a current and valid Nevada driver's license or Nevada identification card showing the voter's residential address, or use the additional proof-of-residency documents permitted by state law when the identification does not show the current address.
deadlines.glance_value: Same-day registration available through Election Day
deadlines.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Registering to Vote
deadlines.internal_note: Current NRS 293.560 permits online registration through Election Day, while NRS 293.5842 and 293.5847 establish same-day registration during early voting and on Election Day. Nevada's 2025 legislation revised portions of these procedures, so current statutory language controls over older voter guides. Same-day registration requires identity and residency verification. This section intentionally emphasizes continued registration availability rather than suggesting that missing the ordinary deadline automatically makes an eligible resident unable to vote.

polling_place.label: Find a Voting Location
polling_place.content: Nevada voters should use the Secretary of State's official voter services or their county election office to find Election Day voting locations and early-voting sites. Nevada counties may operate vote centers that allow eligible county voters to cast a ballot at any designated voting center within the county rather than requiring every voter to use one traditional precinct polling place. Voters should verify locations and hours before voting because they vary by county and election.
polling_place.glance_value: Check state voter services or your county
polling_place.internal_note: Nevada election administration is county-based, and vote-center arrangements can differ by county. Avoid telling every Nevada voter that voting is restricted to a single assigned precinct without checking the county's current system. County election officials publish the authoritative early-voting and Election Day locations.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Nevada's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Election Day voting locations are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. A voter who is waiting in line at 7:00 p.m. must be allowed to vote. Registered Nevada voters generally are not required to present identification merely to cast an ordinary in-person ballot, although identification requirements apply in certain circumstances, including same-day registration. Voters may also return completed mail ballots using authorized methods.
election_day.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Election Day Information
election_day.internal_note: Nevada polling hours are established by NRS 293.273. IMPORTANT: Nevada should not currently be described as a universal photo-ID state. Ordinary registered voters generally do not have to show photo identification simply to vote in person. Same-day registrants have separate identity and residency requirements under NRS 293.5842 and 293.5847.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Nevada Election Day voting locations are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. A voter who is in line at the polling place when polls close at 7:00 p.m. is entitled to vote.
polling_hours.internal_note: NRS 293.273 establishes the 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. Election Day schedule and provides that voters waiting to vote at closing time must be allowed to cast their ballots.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Nevada provides in-person early voting before the General Election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the statutory early-voting period begins Saturday, October 17 and ends Friday, October 30. Eligible residents may also use same-day registration or update their registration at an early-voting location during this period. Exact early-voting locations and operating hours are established and published by county election officials.
early_voting.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Early Voting Information
early_voting.internal_note: Under NRS 293.3568, early voting for a general election begins on the 17th day before Election Day and ends on the fourth day before Election Day. For Tuesday, November 3, 2026, those dates are Saturday, October 17 and Friday, October 30. County clerks establish sites and schedules within statutory requirements. Same-day registration during early voting is authorized by NRS 293.5842.

absentee_mail.label: Mail Ballot Voting
absentee_mail.content: Nevada generally mails a ballot automatically to every active registered voter for statewide elections unless the voter has opted out of receiving mail ballots. A voter does not need to provide an excuse to vote by mail. Completed mail ballots may be returned by mail or through other authorized return methods provided by election officials. A mailed ballot must be postmarked on or before Election Day and received by the county clerk no later than 5:00 p.m. on the fourth day after Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, that statutory receipt deadline falls on Saturday, November 7. A mail ballot whose postmark cannot be determined may still qualify if it is received by 5:00 p.m. on the third day after Election Day under Nevada law.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Automatically mailed to most active registered voters
absentee_mail.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Mail Ballot Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: NRS 293.269911 requires county and city clerks to send mail ballots to active registered voters except those who opt out or fall within statutory exceptions. NRS 293.269921 establishes the Election Day postmark and fourth-day 5:00 p.m. receipt rule and the special third-day rule when a postmark cannot be determined. Nevada's universal-mail system should not be called absentee-only voting.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: A Nevada voter whose registration is current generally does not have to present photo identification simply to cast an ordinary in-person ballot. Election officials verify voters through the procedures required by Nevada election law. Identification and proof-of-residency requirements apply in specific situations. In particular, a person registering in person during early voting or on Election Day must generally present a current and valid Nevada driver's license or Nevada identification card. If that document does not show the voter's current residential address, Nevada law permits specified additional documents showing the current address to establish residency.
voter_id.glance_value: No general photo ID requirement; ID required for same-day registration
voter_id.internal_note: Do not confuse proposed Nevada voter-ID measures with enacted law. As of August 30, 2026, Nevada does not impose a universal photo-ID requirement on every already-registered voter casting an ordinary in-person ballot. NRS 293.5842 and 293.5847 impose Nevada driver's-license/state-ID and residency-document requirements for same-day registration. The 2025 Legislature amended same-day registration procedures, so this section should be reverified if any later court ruling or statutory change occurs before Election Day.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Nevada voters with disabilities have the right to accessible voting and assistance. Polling locations must provide accessible voting systems that allow voters with disabilities to vote privately and independently. A voter who needs help because of a physical disability or inability to read or write may receive assistance, subject to applicable legal restrictions. Nevada also provides an electronic system through which eligible voters with disabilities may receive and mark a ballot electronically. The completed ballot must be returned according to Nevada's required procedures.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment, assistance and electronic ballot access
accessible_voting.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: Nevada law provides accessible voting equipment and voter assistance and establishes an electronic system for certain voters with disabilities under NRS Chapter 293. The electronic system is an accessibility mechanism and should not be described as unrestricted online voting for the general electorate.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Nevada provides special registration and ballot procedures for eligible members of the Uniformed Services, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as a backup when applicable. Nevada also provides an Effective Absentee System for Elections, known as EASE, that allows eligible military and overseas voters to receive and mark election materials electronically and return them using methods authorized by Nevada law. Military and overseas voters should use Nevada's dedicated UOCAVA guidance because their registration and ballot procedures differ from ordinary domestic mail voting.
military_overseas.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Uniformed and Overseas Citizens
military_overseas.internal_note: Nevada implements UOCAVA procedures and operates EASE for eligible military and overseas voters. EASE is also used for certain voters with disabilities. Avoid applying ordinary universal-mail-ballot deadlines or procedures to UOCAVA voters without checking the dedicated rules.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Nevada if they meet Nevada's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A student who establishes a qualifying Nevada residence may register using that residence. A student who remains legally domiciled at another qualifying residence may continue voting from that residence under the applicable state's rules. Students should maintain only one voting residence for an election and should update their voter registration when they establish a new voting residence.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may register at one qualifying voting residence
student_voting.source_name: Nevada Secretary of State — Registering to Vote
student_voting.internal_note: Nevada's general voter-residency requirements govern students. No current Secretary of State student-specific page was relied upon for additional claims. The reader-facing language therefore does not imply that simply attending a Nevada college automatically establishes Nevada voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Nevada county election officials provide sample ballots and voter-specific election information before the General Election. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's residence, precinct and electoral districts, voters should use their county election office or Nevada's official voter services to review the contests and questions that apply to their address. The November 2026 ballot should be checked again after candidate and ballot-question certification is complete.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check official state and county voter services
sample_ballot.internal_note: Nevada counties administer voter-specific sample-ballot distribution and election information. Because the General Election ballot can continue changing through certification deadlines, this section should be reverified close to Election Day rather than presenting a static August sample ballot as final.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Nevada Secretary of State, Elections Division. Carson City office: 101 North Carson Street, Suite 3, Carson City, NV 89701. Main Secretary of State phone: 775-684-5708. Toll-free: 1-800-992-0900. For voter-specific questions involving registration, mail ballots, early-voting locations or Election Day voting locations, voters should also contact their county election office.
contact.internal_note: Nevada elections are administered locally by county election officials under statewide election law and Secretary of State oversight. No email address was inserted into reader-facing content without sufficiently current verification. Contact information should be rechecked if the Secretary of State reorganizes office locations or election contact numbers.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Nevada Secretary of State Elections website and Nevada's official voter registration system for statewide voter information. County election offices administer voter registration records, early-voting locations, Election Day voting locations, mail-ballot processing and many other election functions. Voters should use their county election office for local voting locations and voter-specific questions.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State, RegisterToVoteNV & county election offices
official_resources.internal_note: Official Nevada Elections site: [https://www.nvsos.gov/sos/elections](https://www.nvsos.gov/sos/elections). Official online voter registration: [https://registertovote.nv.gov/](https://registertovote.nv.gov/). Official Nevada statutes: [https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-293.html](https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-293.html). Same-day registration remains available under current Nevada law during early voting and Election Day. Nevada generally mails ballots automatically to active registered voters who have not opted out. All source_url values in this record are bare URL strings, and reader-facing content contains no Markdown hyperlink or mailto syntax.
